claims.statement: The European Commission says more than 80% of the investment needed for building renovation must be mobilized from private capital, including lenders, specialist companies, and building owners.

EU guidance defines energy-performance contracting around improvement that is verified and monitored over the contract term and explicitly references measurement-and-verification methodologies and quality assurance.

contrary_evidence: Banks may treat small retrofit loans as too low-value to justify richer evidence workflows.
EPCs and utility data remain fragmented nationally, limiting standardization.

economics.acquisition_route: Use installer-generated packets to demonstrate the workflow, then pilot through a green-loan broker or leasing intermediary before a direct bank contract.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 20000 projects yearly at 450 PLN blended net revenue produce 9m PLN annual revenue; at 28% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 60% founder ownership, equity is about 6.0m PLN in year 6-9. Retained earnings are not counted separately.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 12-18 hours weekly until a funded pilot; specialist security and energy-audit work is contracted only after revenue.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 70-82% after document processing, telemetry, support, and periodic manual exception review.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 80000-150000 PLN account acquisition and compliance cost recovered after roughly 250-400 funded projects; the initial bootstrap stops before any unfunded bank-scale build.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 400-900 PLN per activated loan plus 10-25 PLN monthly for monitored projects, with volume discounts.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Multi-year monitoring and portfolio reporting create repeat revenue; each new funded project adds another paid event.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A normalized corpus of project documents, missing-evidence patterns, and post-install anomalies reduces verification effort
fingerprint.customer: Banks and leasing firms financing residential or SME energy retrofits
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Lenders and their installer or broker networks make the evidence workflow part of loan fulfillment
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Evidence ingestion, audit trail, exception flags, and portfolio reporting API without underwriting or savings certification
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Lender pays an activation fee per funded project and optionally a monthly monitoring fee
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A retrofit loan is originated or reaches a milestone that requires proof of eligibility, installation, or performance

founder_fit: Combines finance-oriented thinking with data pipelines and renewable-energy domain access.
The family business can create realistic project packets before any lender integration.
API economics and concentrated institutional distribution avoid constant consumer selling.
risks: Bank security and procurement reviews can exceed a bootstrapper's runway.
Poor meter or document data may make measured outcomes misleading.
Product claims could create certification or professional-liability exposure.

structure.control_point: Immutable pre/post retrofit evidence record used in loan fulfillment and portfolio reporting
structure.critical_dependency: A financing partner that recognizes a lower verification cost or reporting benefit

thesis: Sell lenders and leasing firms a narrow evidence rail for energy-retrofit finance: collect installer documents, bills, EPC fields, and device telemetry; produce a traceable pre/post project file; and flag missing or contradictory evidence. It does not certify savings or make credit decisions. The lender distributes it with each loan and benefits from lower verification cost, clearer green-product reporting, and earlier detection of failed installations.
title: Retrofit Loan Evidence Rail
uncertainties: Which Polish green-loan or leasing product has the most expensive manual evidence process?
Whether lenders will pay per funded project or require the installer to pay.
What minimum data set predicts post-installation problems without making regulated credit decisions?
